subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook/skill and sandbox containment checks for the Windows lstat fix carried by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85264?
rationale: The code path is security-sensitive because stale realpath answers could weaken containment if the cache lifetime is too broad; automation should not decide that policy tradeoff even though the linked PR is narrower than the original process-wide cache proposal.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
options.body: Land the linked PR or a maintainer replacement after confirming one caller-owned cache per hook, skill, bind-validation, and sandbox path-resolution operation is the desired security/performance tradeoff.

options.title: Limit optimization to non-containment paths
options.body: Reject cache reuse in containment checks and keep Windows lstat improvements to plugin metadata or other non-boundary hot paths.

options.title: Define a narrower cache contract first
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers document the exact allowed cache lifetime for plugin and sandbox realpath checks.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR or a maintainer replacement after confirming one caller-owned cache per hook, skill, bind-validation, and sandbox path-resolution operation is the desired security/performance tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged manifest-registry realpath-cache follow-up and has recent history on the adjacent cache-lifetime boundary.
